requirements.name: Strong React and TypeScript
requirements.why: Both in every role and in skills.

requirements.name: Writing and reviewing SQL against a relational database
spans: Comfort writing and reviewing SQL against a relational database.
requirements.why: PostgreSQL schema work and SQL in skills.

requirements.name: GraphQL schema design, or a clear appetite to learn it fast
spans: Experience with GraphQL schema design, or a clear appetite to learn it fast.
requirements.why: Rules 6 and 13: the appetite clause is a second way to satisfy one required item, and a CV cannot show appetite. The CV has no GraphQL, so the item is not shown, not missing.

requirements.name: Familiarity with infrastructure as code
spans: Familiarity with infrastructure as code; you will be reading Terraform in your first month even if you do not write much of it.
requirements.why: Docker only; no Terraform or any IaC tool.

requirements.name: A testing habit, whatever the framework
spans: A testing habit, whatever the framework.
requirements.why: Mocha, Supertest, Playwright; integration tests kept under four minutes.

requirements.name: Healthcare or another regulated domain
spans: Experience in healthcare or another regulated domain.

requirements.name: Cypress specifically
requirements.why: Playwright, not Cypress; the posting says specifically.

requirements.name: An eye for accessibility, especially for older users
spans: An eye for accessibility, especially for older users.
requirements.why: Rule 13: 'an eye for' is a trait. Nothing in the CV speaks to it; accessibility work could have shown it, so missing is defensible too.

notRequirements.span: React and TypeScript on the front end.
Node.js services behind a GraphQL gateway.
PostgreSQL, with schema changes reviewed by the whole team.
Jest for unit tests, Cypress for end-to-end.
A take-home exercise you will be paid for, then two conversations: one technical, one about how you work. No whiteboard algorithms.
